subject: Northbridge PHI handling: technical clarifications & BAA next steps
messages:
From: Dr. Susan Keller <s.keller@northbridgehealth.org>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@northbridgehealth.org>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up: PHI handling clarifications (Northbridge)

Evelyn / Redwood team,

Thanks for submitting the initial RFP response last week. The review team had a few technical clarifications we need answered to proceed to legal review and BAA negotiation by the end of next week. Can you please provide short, specific answers to the items below by EOD Monday, 6/22? We can set up a 30-min call if helpful.

1) Where is PHI processed vs stored when customers use Redwood-hosted endpoints? Please include regions and any cross-region replication.
2) Who holds the encryption keys for at-rest PHI in hosted deployments? If Redwood holds them, do you offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
3) Do you perform any model training or fine-tuning on customer data? If so, explain opt-ins and data retention.
4) Retention defaults and controls for chat/engagement logs containing PHI. How can a customer enforce deletion?
5) Can you provide the SOC 2 Type II report, and a short list of third-party subservice providers that handle PHI (cloud infra, monitoring, logging)?

Attachments: Northbridge_RFP_Sections_3-4.pdf (referenced).

Appreciate concise answers — we will summarize for our security team.

Regards,
Susan Keller
Director, Procurement
Northbridge Health

--
Dr. Susan Keller
Northbridge Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Susan Keller <s.keller@northbridgehealth.org>, Procurement Team <procurement@northbridgehealth.org>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: PHI handling clarifications (Northbridge)

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. Answers below (concise) and attached supporting artifacts: redacted_dataflow_diagram.pdf and hipaa-readiness-summary.xlsx. We’ve also attached a proposed BAA draft for initial redlines (proposed_baa_draft.pdf).

1) Processing vs storage: PHI is processed in the region you select at provisioning (we support us-west-2 and us-east-1 for hosted today). Storage (blob + KV cache snapshots) is region-scoped by default; we do not replicate PHI cross-region unless customer enables cross-region backup. We will note the exact provisioning region on the account manifest.

2) Key custody: By default Redwood manages envelope keys in our KMS backed by cloud provider HSMs (tenant-specific key wrapping). We offer customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS and a Bring-Your-Own-Key option for Dedicated/Private customers. In hosted, customers can elect CMK during onboarding; otherwise Redwood holds the key encrypting the data-encryption-key.

3) Model training/fine-tuning: Redwood does NOT train or fine-tune models on customer PHI for hosted or dedicated deployments. Any research or aggregate telemetry is de-identified and requires explicit opt-in. We can provide a contractual clause to prohibit training on customer content.

4) Retention / deletion: Default retention for logs/chat transcripts is 90 days; customers can configure retention to 0/7/30/90/365 days via the Console or API. Deletion requests are enforced at the object store layer and are auditable via the audit log export. For legal holds we can flag retention exceptions but the customer retains control over legal holds.

5) SOC 2 / Subprocessors: We can share an access-controlled SOC 2 Type II report under NDA — please confirm the recipient list. Primary subprocessors: Cloud infra (Amazon Web Services), Monitoring (Datadog), Logs (S3 + managed logging pipeline). Full list is in the attachment.

Next steps: If the answers look good, I can circulate the BAA draft for redlines via DocuSign. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call Friday.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Procurement Team <procurement@northbridgehealth.org>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dr. Susan Keller <s.keller@northbridgehealth.org>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: PHI handling clarifications (Northbridge)

Evelyn — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments. Two quick follow-ups before we move to legal: 

A) KMS detail: when CMK is enabled in hosted, do customers hold the root key material (BYOK) in their HSM, or do you integrate via AWS KMS key policies? We need explicit language on whether Redwood can ever access the unwrapped keys.
B) SOC2: we will execute an NDA to receive the SOC 2 Type II. Please send the access link and point person for the report.

Also, our security engineer asked: is there an option to disable prefix caching for certain endpoints that handle high-sensitivity PHI? We prefer explicit controls rather than global settings.

We are prepared to review the BAA; please route via DocuSign to legal@northbridgehealth.org.

Thanks,
Northbridge Procurement

--
Procurement Team
Northbridge Health
procurement@northbridgehealth.org
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: NBH BAA redlines + tech follow-ups

Eve / Priyom — quick internal note after reading the external thread and attachments. Summary and proposed replies below; please confirm before I send to Susan: 

- CMK behavior: Clarify that customers retain key control via AWS KMS customer-managed CMKs; Redwood cannot obtain plaintext DEKs without a policy exception (we should provide explicit key-policy language). Suggest we offer an audited key-usage report as an extra assurance.
- Prefix caching: Product supports per-endpoint cache toggles. Priyom, can you confirm the API flag name and expected latency impact so I can put numbers in the reply? (sensitive-endpoint-cache=false ?)
- SOC 2 distribution: we'll request the NDA template and provision via secure link. Legal prefers we gate SOC2 by approved recipient list.

Redlines for the BAA: I highlighted three items in proposed_baa_draft.pdf — acceptable defaults, plus a clause to prohibit model training on customer content. Legal will probably want small edits around indemnities; I think we can accept most of their standard language with one technical carve-out for telemetry.

Action items: Priyom to confirm cache flag & latency impact (by EOD). Evelyn to approve the DocuSign route and confirm language around key custody. Once we have that, I will send a single consolidated reply to procurement and route the BAA via DocuSign to legal@northbridgehealth.org.

Thanks — Marcus
